title: Inspect and extend: A client opens a socket and speaks DDP messages
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/chat.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve socket abstraction, connect/session, method ids, ping/pong, timeout and close.
problem: A protocol client is a translator that sends structured envelopes and waits for matching replies. Follow connect, request IDs, timeouts, and ping handling through the fake-socket tests. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/chat.ts` and the related project files: src/chat.ts; test/chat.test.ts.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to socket abstraction, connect/session, method ids, ping/pong, timeout and close.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The app-specific methods channels.list, chat.sendMessage, and chat.getMessages are not verified Rocket.Chat method names; DDP method calls are marked deprecated in current Rocket.Chat documentation.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A protocol client is a translator that sends structured envelopes and waits for matching replies. Follow connect, request IDs, timeouts, and ping handling through the fake-socket tests.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/chat.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
